English copy — v1.4 review: THE CHALLENGE
A photo shows the problem. It rarely explains it.

A photo may show water damage or a dirty coil without identifying where it was found, which checks were performed or what the next person needs to know. Field teams may have to reconstruct details from scattered photos, notes and recollections after a visit.
Internal note / approval: Fanyao has owner interviews, not technician study

English copy — v1.4 review: Gaps a pilot is designed to test:
Missing context. Photos may lack a location, equipment identity or corresponding check.
Extra reporting work. Teams may have to piece together details after a visit.
Unclear handoffs. A reviewer may struggle to tell what is confirmed and what remains uncertain.
WHY WEARABLE
Designed around the way field work happens.

Field work can occupy both hands and take technicians into tight or awkward spaces. HA-VEST01 explores whether a body-worn approach can reduce the need to interrupt a task to handle a separate recording device while preserving useful job context.
Internal note / approval: Value hypothesis; no proven hands-free claim

English copy — v1.4 review: COMMON QUESTIONS
Is HA-VEST01 available for full deployment? — Not yet. Evaluation scope and availability are confirmed project by project.
Does it diagnose problems or produce final reports by itself? — It is not presented as an autonomous diagnosis or final reporting system. Qualified professionals retain diagnosis and final review.
What are its weight and battery life? — These depend on the agreed configuration and operating mode and must be verified against prototype tests.
What about privacy and capture permissions? — Permission, data handling and any image treatment must be defined and tested for the specific project. There is no universal automatic guarantee.
Who owns and can access the records? — Data ownership, visibility and access permissions must be agreed and validated for each project.
How do we start? — Tell us about one recurring job and the record your team needs. We can discuss whether a scoped evaluation makes sense.
